trip_note: 9 days, early March 2027, EXACTLY FIVE people flying from Buenos Aires. Lima 2 nights (Barranco) + Mancora 5 nights + Lima transit home. All prices USD. GROUP MATH: every hotel below is priced for all five people in a real, bookable room configuration - see rooms_for_5 and group_night_usd. pp_night_usd = group_night_usd / 5 and the budget test is pp_night_usd <= 100, i.e. up to ~USD 500/night for the group. Airbnbs are priced for the whole house divided by five. SINGLE-ROOM ASSUMPTION: Peruvian boutique hotels rarely discount a double to single occupancy by more than 20-30%, so where a config uses a fifth bed in a third room I have assumed the third room costs 80-100% of a double and said so. NO price here is a confirmed March-2027 quote - nothing publishes rates 18 months out - so every hotel is is_estimate true, taken from current (Sept 2026) Booking.com listing pages and hotel official sites. Early March is HIGH season on the north coast; budget +15-30% on top. PRIORITY APPLIED: design and architecture first, then value, then price.

stops.name: Lima
stops.area_note: Barranco is the right call: clifftop, walkable, street art, with Hotel B / MATE / Pedro de Osma / Central / Kjolle / Isolina / Merito / Lady Bee all inside ~15 blocks, and the Miraflores malecon a 25-min walk or 10-min taxi north. Miraflores has more hotel stock but is comparatively corporate. Airport (LIM) to Barranco is 45-70 min, USD 20-30 by Uber/Cabify. FOR FIVE PEOPLE, TWO NIGHTS: three rooms is the realistic ask, and Barranco's best places are small (Second Home has 8 rooms, Hotel B has 17, Atemporal has 9), so three rooms on the same March dates needs booking months out. An entire Barranco house on Airbnb is cheaper per head but you lose the architecture - and for only two nights in Lima the hotel is worth it. HONESTY FLAG: Booking.com individual hotel pages return empty to automated fetches, so scores and prices come from Booking.com's Barranco district page and Lima design-hotels page (both fetched 2026-09-20) plus hotel official sites. Two Barranco Booking.com slugs could not be confirmed, so a Booking.com search URL is given and flagged.

Booking.com's district page showed USD 128.25 for a double, consistent with the direct rates. Verified operating with positive reviews from June 2025; owner Lilian Delfin runs it, her father the sculptor still lives on site. ONLY 8 ROOMS - three of them on the same March dates is the single biggest booking risk in this whole plan. Email secondhomeperu@gmail.com / +51 1 246 4615 and book direct.

Less architecturally distinctive than Second Home or Casa Republica - this is the value line, not the design line.

hotels.name: Hotel B
hotels.area: Barranco - Av. Saenz Pena 204, next door to MATE
hotels.rating: 5-star, Relais & Chateaux, 17 rooms in a 1914 Belle Epoque mansion
hotels.rooms_for_5: 3 rooms: 2 doubles + 1 as a single. 17 rooms, so capacity is fine but availability in March is not.
hotels.why: Belle Epoque mansion run as a living contemporary art gallery; Lima's best-looking hotel.
hotels.note: WAY OVER BUDGET: USD 214 pp/night, more than double the cap. Group total = 3 x USD 356. Built 1914, hotel since May 2013, Peru's only Relais & Chateaux, art collection curated across the whole building. If the group wants one showpiece night in Lima this is the one to blow it on - but doing it for both nights costs more than five nights in Mancora. Atemporal by Andean in Miraflores (9 rooms, 9.6-9.8 scores, ~USD 300+/room) is the other hotel at this level; Barranco Boutique Hotel by 3B (9.3/10, USD 82.50/room, 3 rooms = USD 248 / USD 50 pp) is the plain-but-clean budget fallback if everything above is full.

activities.what: Ride the 10km clifftop cycle path past Parque del Amor and Larcomar to Chorrillos and back.

Street rate has historically been around S/300-400 (USD 80-110) paid at the launch site in Parque Raimondi. Flights go one at a time, so allow 1-2 hours for the group to cycle through. Confirm on the day - it is wind-dependent.

activities.what: One of the world's-50-best Peruvian tasting menus. Kjolle shares a building with Central in Barranco.
activities.note: VERIFIED from official sites and 2026 sources: Kjolle tasting menu S/988 (~USD 264 pp, ~USD 1,320 for five), vegetal version S/456 (~USD 122). Maido 'Maido Experience' S/1,295 (~USD 340 pp), pairings S/1,985-2,525. Mayta Experience S/899 (~USD 240 pp), a la carte USD 50-100. Central quotes varied USD 267-440 pp across sources - treat as USD 300-440. BOOKING FOR FIVE: Central and Maido need 1-3 months' notice and a table for five is harder than a table for two; Maido was named World's Best Restaurant 2025. KJOLLE OR MAYTA ARE THE SMART PICKS for a group of five - same kitchens' quality, a third of the hassle, and Kjolle is a 10-min walk from any Barranco hotel.

stops.weather_note: Early March is the tail of Lima's summer and the best weather of the year: highs around 26-28C, nights 19-20C, high humidity (70-85%), strong UV, and essentially no rain - Lima is a coastal desert and the grey garua drizzle is a May-October phenomenon, not a March one. The sea is at its annual warmest but the Humboldt current still keeps it cool, roughly 20-22C, so the malecon beaches are swimmable-but-bracing rather than tropical. HONESTY: the web-search budget ran out before a Lima March climate page could be fetched, so these figures come from general climate knowledge rather than a page fetched in this pass - sanity-check on weather-and-climate.com or senamhi.gob.pe before packing.

stops.name: Mancora (Piura / Tumbes north coast)
stops.area_note: The strip runs north to south: Punta Sal / Canoas (25-45 min north, wide and calm) - Mancora town (the party and the point break) - Las Pocitas (2km south, rock tide pools, the boutique hotels) - Vichayito (5-10 min further south, emptiest sand, whole-house rentals) - Los Organos (10-15 min south, fishing village, the advanced left called La Vuelta) - El Nuro (the turtle pier) - Cabo Blanco (40 min south, Hemingway's old fishing club and a world-class barrel on north swells). LAS POCITAS AND VICHAYITO ARE THE RIGHT BASE: beautiful, quiet, and a S/5-15 mototaxi from Mancora's restaurants and bars, so you get the scene without sleeping in it. FOR FIVE PEOPLE OVER FIVE NIGHTS, A WHOLE HOUSE IN LAS POCITAS OR VICHAYITO IS THE BEST VALUE ON THIS ENTIRE TRIP and it is also where the good architecture is - the strip's best buildings are private beach houses, not hotels. A 4-5 bedroom beachfront house at USD 280-400 a night works out at USD 56-80 pp, beats every hotel here on space and privacy, gives you a kitchen and a pool, and is the single strongest recommendation in this file. Hotels are the better call only if nobody wants to cook or drive. GETTING THERE from Lima: fly LIM to Talara (TYL, ~1h from Mancora), Tumbes (TBP, ~1h30) or Piura (PIU, ~2h30) on LATAM or Sky, then a pre-booked private transfer (USD 40-60 for the car from Talara, which splits five ways nicely) or a colectivo. HONESTY FLAG: Booking.com individual hotel pages return empty to automated fetches, so scores and prices come from Booking.com's Mancora, Vichayito, Los Organos and Canoas de Punta Sal city pages plus the Mancora design-hotels page, all fetched 2026-09-20, cross-checked against hotel official sites. Where a Booking.com slug could not be confirmed, a search or city URL is given and flagged.

activities.note: Free to do; USD 15 covers ceviche and beers. Check the tide table - the 'pocitas' only form at low tide, which is what the beach is named for.

activities.name: Surf lesson at the Mancora point break
activities.what: Long, mellow left reef break; the inside section is one of South America's best beginner waves.
activities.when: Early morning, 07:00-09:00, before the afternoon wind
activities.note: VERIFIED price range: group lessons S/60-100 (USD 16-27) for 1-2 hours; private 80-min lessons around S/50 at some schools; board rental S/20-40/hour, S/30-50 half day, S/50-80 full day. Five people is two instructors' worth - book the day before. Mancora point works essentially year-round at 1-2.5m and gets crowded. Schools: Mancora Kite Club, Surf Point Mancora, Inca Warriors.

activities.name: Poza de Barro mud baths plus Mirador de Mancora
activities.what: Sulfurous thermal mud pool up the Fernandez valley, 11km inland, reached by mototaxi.
activities.note: VERIFIED: entrance S/5-15 (USD 1.50-4) if you go alone by mototaxi (~35 min each way; five people need two or three mototaxis). Organised tours with hotel pickup, transfer, guide and the Mirador viewpoint run roughly USD 25-35 pp for 2h30. Also reachable on horseback (2h) or on foot (4h). GetYourGuide and Civitatis product pages return 403 to automated fetches, so the tour price is a range estimate.

activities.name: Horseback ride along Vichayito beach at sunset
activities.what: Ride several kilometres of empty sand between Mancora and Vichayito in the golden hour.
activities.note: VERIFIED price: TraviTour lists the coastal horse ride at S/60 list, S/40 sale (USD 11-17). Finca Capitan Mancora (fincacapitanmancora.com) also runs guided rides. Five horses in the sunset slot needs booking a day or two ahead - it is the most-requested time.

activities.name: Swim with green sea turtles at El Nuro pier
activities.what: Wild green turtles gather under the fishing pier for scraps; you snorkel among them from a small boat.
activities.when: Morning, 08:00-11:00 (pier open 08:00-17:00, calmest and clearest early)
activities.note: VERIFIED DIY cost: pier entry S/5, swim-with-turtles boat S/10-15, compulsory life jacket S/2, optional snorkel S/5 - about USD 6-8 all in, plus transport from Mancora (20km, S/15-25 by mototaxi or a shared taxi for five). Organised 3-hour tours from Mancora start around S/100 (USD 27), rising to USD 45 for catamaran versions; a group of five fills a small boat, so negotiate a private one. SEASON HONESTY: one regional guide lists 'sea turtle swimming: June-Oct', but the El Nuro turtles are resident year-round because they follow the fishing boats, and most operators run daily all year. Confirm with your hotel the week before.

activities.name: Lunch in Los Organos and the La Vuelta left
activities.what: Fishing-village lunch, then watch or surf the powerful tubular left reef called La Vuelta.
activities.note: SEASON: VERIFIED GOOD FOR MARCH. La Vuelta works on north swells, October to April, up to 2.5m with multiple tube sections - described as one of the best waves in Peru. Advanced only; anyone who learned at Mancora point three days earlier should watch, not paddle out.

activities.name: Day trip north to Punta Sal / Canoas
activities.what: The strip's widest, calmest, emptiest beach, 25-45 min north in the Tumbes region.
activities.note: Colectivo along the Panamericana is S/10-15 each way (USD 3-4); a private taxi that takes all five is USD 40-60 return, which is USD 8-12 each and far easier. Lunch on the beach USD 15-25. If you want a night there, El Samay Hotel Boutique in Canoas scores 9.8/10 across ~220 Booking.com reviews at about USD 100 a room.

activities.name: Cabo Blanco: Hemingway's fishing club and the barrel
activities.what: Forty minutes south; the 1950s big-game fishing club site and a world-famous tubing left.
activities.note: TWO HONESTY FLAGS. (1) SURF: verified good for March - Cabo Blanco is a left reef break working on north swells October to April, up to 3m, 'world famous for its long, perfect tubes', but it only truly breaks about 8 times a year and is advanced-only. (2) DEEP-SEA FISHING: Cabo Blanco is NO LONGER an organised sportfishing destination. Hemingway fished here in 1956 and Alfred Glassell's 1,560lb black marlin all-tackle world record still stands from 1953, but current sources describe basic facilities and limited organised charters - you negotiate directly with local boats. Expect USD 250-450 for a boat for the day, cash, arranged through your hotel; split five ways that is USD 50-90 each and a boat comfortably takes five. Peru-wide charters on FishingBooker start around USD 245. NONE OF THESE FISHING FIGURES IS A CONFIRMED QUOTE.

activities.name: Kitesurfing lesson - ONLY IF THE WIND SHOWS UP
activities.what: Mobile schools cover Mancora, Pocitas, Vichayito, Los Organos and El Nuro and come to your house.
activities.when: Afternoon, 11:00-17:00 when the thermal wind builds
activities.note: SEASON HONESTY - MARCH IS THE WRONG MONTH. Verified: the Mancora kite season runs roughly April/May to December, with the most constant wind in August, September and October. Early March sits at the bottom of the wind cycle. Keep this as an opportunistic 'if it is blowing' item, not a planned day. VERIFIED prices when it does run: USD 245 for a 6-hour semi-private beginner course, USD 360 for three afternoons of private lessons; a local guide quotes S/200-350 for single lessons.

activities.name: Last-day slow plan: SUP or snorkel, then sunset drinks in Mancora
activities.what: Paddleboard the flat Vichayito water in the morning, then the Mancora beach bars for sunset.
activities.note: SUP rental roughly S/40-60/hour (USD 11-16) from hotels along Vichayito and Pocitas. Mancora's beach bars are lively but not a party-hostel scene before ~22:00; after that the main drag gets loud, which is exactly why sleeping in Pocitas or Vichayito is the right call.

activities.name: WHALE WATCHING - NOT AVAILABLE IN MARCH
activities.what: Humpbacks migrating from Antarctica to calve off Los Organos, Punta Sal and Mancora.
activities.note: CLEAR NO. Multiple independent sources confirm the season starts mid-July and ends late October. Early March is four months outside it and there will be no humpbacks. Listed here only so nobody in the group books a March 'whale tour' from an operator happy to take the money. When it does run it costs S/80-150 (USD 22-40) for 2-3 hours from Los Organos. Day 0 is a deliberate marker, not a trip day.

food.name: La Sirena d'Juan (Mancora, main strip)
food.what: The town's long-standing fine-dining room; Peruvian-Japanese seafood, tiny, so book a table for five ahead.

food.name: At(e)lier (Mancora)
food.what: Dim, atmospheric small plates and craft cocktails; inventive dishes like banana gnocchi, vegan options.
food.price_level: $$$ - higher-end for Mancora, roughly USD 25-45 pp

food.name: Tokuyo (Mancora)
food.what: Mancora's sushi and Nikkei spot; vegan makis and poke bowls as well as the raw fish.

food.name: La Biodega / Blacksheep Cafe (Mancora)
food.what: Daytime cafes for coffee, chai, brunch and working wifi; Blacksheep is air-conditioned and mural-covered.

food.name: Side-street cevicherias (Mancora and Los Organos)
food.what: Ceviche S/20-35, arroz con mariscos S/25-40, grilled fish S/20-30, set lunch (menu) S/10-15.
food.price_level: $ - USD 3-11 pp; far better value than the main strip

stops.weather_note: March is Mancora's hottest month and the best swimming of the year: daytime highs around 30-31C (the national weather service puts the March average high at 30.8C), nights 23-24C, sea temperature around 25C - the warmest it gets - and about 10.6 hours of sun a day. December to April is peak beach season, so early March is hot, sunny and BUSY, with high-season room rates and houses booked months out. THE HONEST CAVEAT: March is also statistically the wettest month on the north coast, averaging around 128mm of rain. That average is heavily skewed by El Nino years; in a normal year you get a handful of short, heavy afternoon downpours and high humidity rather than washed-out days, but it is not the guaranteed-dry month that August is. Pack for heat and humidity, bring reef-safe sunscreen, and do not count on five consecutive cloudless days.

getting_around: MANCORA: mototaxis (tuk-tuks) are the whole transport system. Verified fares: S/2-5 (USD 0.50-1.30) within Mancora town; S/5-10 to Las Pocitas; S/10-15 to Vichayito; S/15-25 to Los Organos or El Nuro. FIVE PEOPLE NEED TWO OR THREE MOTOTAXIS - they take two comfortably, three at a squeeze - so double or triple every fare above, and for anything beyond Los Organos hire a regular taxi for the group instead. Always agree the fare before getting in; prices move with demand and roughly double after midnight. Colectivos (shared vans) run the Panamericana for S/3-8 and are how you reach Punta Sal or Cabo Blanco cheaply. Bicycle rental S/20-30 a day. Mancora town is walkable end to end in 15 minutes, and from Las Pocitas you can walk to town along the beach at low tide in 25-30 minutes. Several Pocitas and Vichayito hotels run free shuttles - ask, and ask whether the shuttle takes five. AIRPORTS: Talara (TYL) ~1h, Tumbes (TBP) ~1h30, Piura (PIU) ~2h30; a private transfer from Talara is roughly USD 40-60 for the car, which is USD 8-12 a head for five and much better than five colectivo seats. Operators include Texa Tours and Talara Express. LIMA: use Uber, Cabify or DiDi rather than street taxis - note that five people plus luggage needs an XL vehicle or two cars. Barranco to Miraflores USD 4-7, Barranco to the airport USD 20-30 and 45-70 minutes depending on traffic. Barranco itself is entirely walkable and the Miraflores malecon is a flat 10km cycle path.
